title: BC land status of a block
description: What land the block is on, and so which law reaches its harvest: whether FRPA’s forest practices reach it (Crown land, or private land in a tree farm licence, community forest agreement or woodlot licence area), whether the WLPPR replaces the FPPR for a woodlot licence holder, whether it is private managed forest land under the PMFLA, and, on private land, timber reserved to the government, boundaries beside Crown land and the Forest Act’s timber marking and scaling. A reserve and treaty settlement land are outside every rule here: the Indian Act, a land code or the final agreement governs them, and none is assessed. The land is always the reviewer’s answer; mapped parcels and licences are candidates.

relatedPacks.relationship: Its findings are the block’s only where FRPA’s forest practices reach the land and the holder is not a woodlot licence holder (frpa-reach, frpa-no-reach, woodlot-wlppr).
Cutting and road permits dispose of Crown timber and roads on Crown land; on private land outside an area-based licence they do not arise unless timber is reserved to the government (crown-timber).
Its rules are the WLPPR’s practice requirements for a woodlot licence holder’s block, applying when woodlot-wlppr does; the land, licence area and woodlot holder questions are shared (sameAs).

choices: Federal land, including an Indian reserve
facts.label: What land is the block on? Crown land is land vested in the provincial government (the Land Act meaning, Forest Act §1); private land is land that is not Crown land. A reserve and treaty settlement land are asked apart: these packs do not assess them.
Is the block in the area of an area-based licence (Forest Act §1), on its Crown land or on private land the licence includes?
Will the woodlot licence holder, or its employee, agent, contractor or subcontractor, carry out the harvest (WLPPR §2(1))?

Is the block’s private land private managed forest land: land under a management commitment and classified as managed forest land under the Assessment Act (PMFLA §1), or land classified as managed forest land when the Act came into force and deemed so without a commitment (§45)?
Is any timber on the block’s private land reserved to the government, by its Crown grant or otherwise (Forest Act §1, “Crown timber”)?
Is the block’s private land adjacent to Crown land (FRPA §53)?

sources.title: Forest and Range Practices Act, SBC 2002 c. 69
BC Forest Planning and Practices Regulation
Woodlot Licence Planning and Practices Regulation, BC Reg 21/2004
Private Managed Forest Land Act, SBC 2003 c. 80

rules.title: FRPA’s forest practices reach the block’s land
rules.finding: A forest practice under FRPA is an activity on Crown forest land, or on private land subject to a tree farm licence, a community forest agreement or a woodlot licence. The block’s land is one of these, so FRPA and its practices regulation reach the harvest: review the block under them.

actions.description: Review the block under FRPA and the practices regulation that applies to its holder: the FPPR, or the WLPPR in a woodlot licence area.

rules.title: FRPA’s forest practices do not reach this private land
rules.finding: FRPA’s definition of a forest practice takes in private land only where a tree farm licence, a community forest agreement or a woodlot licence covers it; a First Nations woodland licence is not named. The block is wholly on private land outside those, so the FPPR findings on this block are not this land’s. The owner’s title, the Forest Act’s timber marking and scaling, and on managed forest land the Private Managed Forest Land Act govern instead. This is a reading of the definition’s text.

actions.description: Read the block’s FPPR, permit and forest operations findings as not applying to this land, and review it under the rules below and, if it is managed forest land, the Private Managed Forest Land Act.

rules.title: The WLPPR, not the FPPR, governs the woodlot licence holder
rules.finding: The Woodlot Licence Planning and Practices Regulation applies to the woodlot licence holder, and the holder’s employees, agents and contractors, carrying out an activity in the woodlot licence area, and the FPPR, except its §1.2, does not apply to them. The FPPR findings on this block are read against a regulation that does not govern its harvest; the woodlot licence practices review (bc.woodlot-practices) assesses the WLPPR’s practice requirements in their place.

actions.description: Review the block against the WLPPR and the holder’s woodlot licence plan, in the woodlot licence practices findings, rather than the FPPR findings.

rules.title: Private managed forest land: the PMFLA’s objectives apply
rules.finding: The block’s private land is private managed forest land outside a tree farm licence, woodlot licence and community forest agreement area, so the Private Managed Forest Land Act applies: its forest management objectives for soil conservation, drinking water, fish habitat, critical wildlife habitat and reforestation (§§12–16) and the Council Regulation’s requirements govern the harvest, not FRPA’s.

actions.description: Review the block against the PMFLA’s objectives and the Private Managed Forest Land Council Regulation; the owner’s management commitment is with the Private Managed Forest Land Council.

rules.title: Timber reserved to the government is Crown timber
rules.finding: Timber reserved to the government is Crown timber although it stands on private land, so cutting it needs an authority to harvest Crown timber under the Forest Act, as on Crown land; the owner cannot grant it.

actions.description: Find the reservation in the title or Crown grant, and hold a Forest Act authority to cut the reserved timber before harvesting it.

rules.title: Private land beside Crown land: ascertain the boundaries
rules.finding: Before anyone cuts or removes timber from private land adjacent to Crown land, they must ascertain the private land’s boundaries, and the owner or occupier who authorizes them must first inform them of the boundaries. Not knowing them is no defence to a prosecution for cutting Crown timber (§94).

actions.description: Have the private land’s boundaries ascertained and marked on the ground before falling, and keep the owner’s notice of them.

rules.title: Timber from private land carries that land’s timber mark
rules.finding: Unscaled timber cut from the block’s private land must be marked in the prescribed manner with a timber mark that pertains to that land before it is removed or transported, and in prescribed circumstances before it is stored in decks or piles there. The registrar issues a timber mark certificate for private land on application (§85).

actions.description: Apply for a timber mark certificate for the private land, unless one in force already pertains to it, and mark the timber before it leaves the land.

exceptions.label: The minister has exempted the unscaled timber from marking, with any conditions (§84(5))
evidence: The minister’s exemption and its conditions

rules.title: Timber from private land is scaled by a licensed scaler
rules.finding: Timber cut from the block’s private land may not be manufactured into products, sold, or transported anywhere but the place it must go for scaling until a licensed scaler authorized by the minister scales it.

actions.description: Arrange scaling by a licensed scaler at the scale site before the timber is sold or manufactured.

exceptions.label: The minister has exempted the timber or the person from scaling, with any conditions (§94(5)–(6))
evidence: The minister’s exemption and its conditions
